courses.title: React Essential Training
courses.why: The current flagship React course by Eve Porcello: components, hooks, Vite and Next, and React Server Components vs Client Components. Fast for an experienced developer and gives an up-to-date certificate.

courses.title: React: Using TypeScript
courses.why: A short course on typing React components and hooks, which most React job descriptions now require.

courses.title: Building Scalable React UI Component Libraries with Storybook
courses.why: The newest of the three: component libraries and design systems, the 'responsive UI component libraries' skill senior front-end JDs ask for.

portals.name: react.dev: Learn React (official)
portals.what: The official guides with interactive challenges on state, effects, refs and 'you might not need an effect'.

portals.name: GreatFrontEnd: React interview questions
portals.what: React-specific front-end interview questions and component-building exercises, many free.

portals.name: roadmap.sh: React questions
portals.what: A bank of React interview questions with short answers for quick self-quizzing.

portals.name: Frontend Mentor challenges
portals.what: Realistic UI designs to build from scratch, good practice for live React component rounds.

assessments.name: JavaScript (Intermediate) certification
assessments.format: 1 hr 30 min online test, 2 coding questions (topics include design patterns)
assessments.credential: HackerRank certificate with a shareable URL
assessments.why: You already hold HackerRank's Frontend Developer (React) role certificate; JavaScript (Intermediate) adds the language depth behind it and is quick to earn.

assessments.name: Software Engineer certification
assessments.format: 1 hr 15 min online test, 3 questions covering problem solving, SQL and REST API
assessments.credential: HackerRank role certificate with a shareable URL
assessments.why: A second role certificate next to your Frontend Developer (React) one, showing full-stack breadth.
